fact: The Autentika page says a citizen may authenticate with the CNI at any Cabo Verdean public administration portal that has joined Autentika, and that any duly authorised application may integrate by OpenID Connect; no date is given, so as_of is the published year (proxy).
The Autentika page states that more than 95,000 users use the platform daily to reach work applications; no count of relying services is given, and the date is the published year (proxy).
The PDEX page says all integrations of the Consular Portal with the civil identification system run through PDEX, giving access to citizens' data; it does not say the portal verifies people.

The Government of Cabo Verde says the Portal de Justiça, launched on 18 December 2024, is integrated with the state's Autentika platform and supports several user authentication methods for services including certificates and online renewal of the CNI.
IMIJ says SNIAC links more than 50 public and private services, with banking foremost.
IMIJ says SNIAC supports the Justice, Consular and National portals and connects public and private services, banks especially.
IMIJ reports more than 30 million data requests recorded on SNIAC and over 50 connected services.

SNIAC published version 1.9.9 of its national ID card middleware on 17 March 2026, with an SDK that lets public or private services integrate their own applications to authenticate the holder, read their data and collect a digital signature; no service using it is named.
